question: Why are test-autohook-session entries landing in chronicle files whose names don't match their session_id (e.g., ~/.sovereign/chronicle/learnings/testing.jsonl contains entries with session_id='test-autohook-session')? record_insight at memory.py:371 writes to '<domain_dir>/<session_id>.jsonl' so filename SHOULD equal session_id. Either there's a separate chronicle-write path that uses a different filename convention, or these entries were appended via raw file write bypassing record_insight. Worth tracing — the discrepancy suggests at least one auto-hook code path writes chronicle entries without going through the canonical primitive. Found while diagnosing the test-session-hook-777 leak (2026-04-29 morning, claude-iphone orchestration brief).
resolution: Root cause: test_nape_autohook.py called _dispatch_tool without patching srv_module.experiential or SPIRAL_STATE_PATH, writing test-autohook-session entries to live ~/.sovereign/chronicle. Fixed with _isolated_server() context manager that patches both to a tempdir. Added TestChronicleFileNaming regression tests. commit 23e10aa.
